title: Connector marketplace preflight: localization, technical gating, and legal terms (draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc is a lightweight preflight for partner connectors or integrations that will be published to cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP and first-party portals). It bundles: localized copy guidance, a technical gating checklist (what the marketplace reviewers will check), legal/terms flags we must surface to partners, and a minimal go-live runbook. Intent: reduce back-and-forth during the listing submission window and capture edge cases for partners with localized/compliance needs.

Audience
- Partner engineering/product managers preparing a listing
- Redwood go-to-market (partner ops + listings) reviewers
- Marketplace ops (internal reviewers and our vendor contacts)

Quick summary (one-liners to use internally)
- Short tagline: "Enterprise LLM inference, deployed where you need it."
- 1-sentence elevator: "Redwood Inference lets teams run high-performance LLMs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with built-in observability and predictable unit economics."

Why localization matters here
Marketplaces increasingly require localized tile copy and legal snippets for key geographies (EN/FR/DE/JP/ES). For partners that want multi-region tiles, we need canonical short+long descriptions plus localized legal callouts (data residency, encryption, support hours). If partner provides only EN, we surface the risk: slower review and reduced visibility in localized storefronts.

Listing copy variants (required deliverables)
1) Tile title (<= 60 chars): concise brand + primary value. Example: "Redwood Inference — Fast, predictable LLM inference"
2) One-line subtitle (<= 120 chars): succinct benefit for discovery. Example: "Low-latency model serving with per-token cost control and enterprise SLAs."
3) Short description (<= 300 chars): used in search results and tiles. 
   - Example: "Serve open and proprietary LLMs with predictable latency and cost — hosted, dedicated, or private deployment options and enterprise-grade monitoring."
4) Long description (300–1500 chars): used on the listing detail page; include product capabilities, supported environments, and primary use cases. Use short paragraphs and bullets.
5) Feature bullets (4–8): short 4–8 items highlighting differentiators (e.g., "Dedicated GPU pools with SLA-backed latency", "Automatic KV-prefix caching and batching", "Private VPC and on-prem packages").
6) Pricing blurb: concise explanation of billing model and any free trial credits. Example: "Usage-based per-token billing. 14-day free trial with $X credits for new marketplace customers. Contact sales for Dedicated pricing."
7) Support & compliance blurb: short summary of SLAs and compliance options (SOC2, EU data residency).
8) Legal callouts (one- or two-line mandatory bullets): data retention, encryption at rest/in-transit, support contact, KMS/HSM availability.

Copy style guidelines (non-negotiable)
- Avoid product-internal jargon (e.g., don’t use internal feature names like "smart-route-3").
- Prefer active voice and customer-centric benefits.
- For localized variants, provide translations as separate files (UTF-8, plain text) and mark any placeholders like {ACCOUNT_NAME} or {REGION} clearly.

Technical gating checklist (what marketplace reviewers will verify)
- Asset hygiene
  - Tile PNG/JPG: required resolutions (verify marketplace-specific asset specs).
  - Favicon / Square tile icon: 1:1 at 1024x1024 recommended.
  - Demo video: hosted link (YouTube/partner CDN) with captions for EN; optional for other locales.
- Functional/Integration proofs
  - Quickstart docs link present: minimal getting-started showing API key creation, a sample request, and expected response.
  - Sandbox/test mode credentials (if partner provides): ephemeral keys and instructions for reviewer testing.
  - If connector uses marketplace SSO or credential exchange (e.g. AWS Marketplace Metering or SaaS contract flow), include a flow diagram + endpoints and a test account.
- Security & compliance checks
  - TLS enforced everywhere; mention TLS versions supported.
  - Data processing locations declared (region-level) and a brief note on data retention defaults.
  - KMS/HSM support notes if customer-managed keys are available.
- Billing integration points
  - Marketplace billing SKU IDs (or a placeholder) must be supplied prior to publication.
  - Trial provisioning behavior documented: how credits are assigned and how trial-to-paid conversion works.
- Operational readiness
  - Support SLAs and contact details for marketplace customers.
  - Observability endpoints: where marketplace telemetry will be sent (internal telemetry + optional partner-supplied hooks).

Legal & compliance flags to surface to partner (high priority)
- Data residency guarantees: clarify if the offering will process data only in the customer’s region. If not, explicitly state processing locations and any cross-border transfer steps.
- Required DPA / Addendum: partners must accept our standard marketplace DPA or provide their own via legal review.
- Export control / restricted content: highlight if the partner product handles regulated data sets (medical, financial) and provide guidance for restricted geos.
- Branding & trademark: tile copy must not include third-party logos without permission; include brand usage guide link.

Marketplace-specific gotchas (short list)
- AWS: metered billing flows sometimes require an account linkage step—test the redirection flow twice.
- Azure: offer categories and SKUs must match the Azure catalog taxonomy or the listing will fail automated categorization.
- GCP: tiles with non-English descriptions may be deprioritized if translations are missing captions for demo video.

Acceptance criteria (internal checklist before submission)
- All copy fields provided (title, subtitle, short, long) in target locales OR an explicit single-locale waiver.
- All required assets present and validated against vendor specs.
- Sandbox test case that demonstrates a minimal request/response within 3 steps.
- Billing SKU or commerce placeholder assigned and documented.
- Legal DPA status flagged: "partner-signed", "partner-pending", or "partner-provided (needs review)".

Preflight runbook (high-level steps)
1) Partner completes the "listing intake" form (link included in intake doc).
2) GTM reviewer verifies assets and copy; returns list of deficits via intake ticket (GO-4321).
3) Engineering partner-success verifies SSO/billing integration and provides sandbox credentials.
4) Legal runs DPA review in parallel; flag blocking items.
5) Once green, we schedule a 1-hour submission window with vendor onboarding contact and walk the partner through the submission flow (record session).
6) Post-submission: monitor the marketplace listing status and address reviewer comments within 48 hours.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Translation ownership: do we expect partners to supply translations, or will Redwood provide a vetted translation service (cost + SLA)?
- Trial credit amount: standardize X credits per new marketplace user (proposal: $200) or leave partner to choose?
- Localization priority: which geos get first-class support for tile placement (US/EU/JP)?

Next steps
- Mateo to compile asset spec links for the three major marketplaces (due 2025-01-22).
- Elaine to draft the minimal legal blurb templates for tile copy (due 2025-01-24).
- Samir to create the intake form and wire it to GO-4321 (draft by 2025-01-20).

Notes to self / fragments (work-in-progress)
- Consider a "localization waiver" checkbox on intake: partner opts for EN-only listing for initial publication.
- Slack thread with vendor contact: #marketplace-onboarding with subject "Azure tile failure types".

Appendix: sample localized short description (EN -> DE placeholder)
- EN: "Serve open and proprietary LLMs with predictable latency and cost — hosted, dedicated, or private."
- DE (placeholder translation to be provided by partner or vendor): "Bereitstellen offener und proprietärer LLMs mit vorhersehbarer Latenz und Kosten — gehostet, dediziert oder privat."

If you want a trimmed checklist CSV or a slide-ready one-pager for partners, say which marketplace and I'll produce it as a separate artifact.
